content.thinking:
I'm planning the kraken design in one careful pass: a rising sea creature with a domed mantle, head, eyes, and a mix of eight shorter tentacles plus two long ones, styled with clean bold Overwatch-like shapes and panel lines. I'm deciding on a deep indigo-blue body with a glowing orange accent for contrast.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton structure -- a root core joint with a mantle chain rising upward, a forward head with beak parts, and eight tentacle chains parented to the core, each defined as a curved path arcing from the body down to the floor where tips rest, plus a water splash disc for floor contact.

Adding head joint and core sphere, then sweeping the mantle body along its chain, and placing glowing eye spheres on the head sides using world-space positioning to avoid local axis confusion.

Flattening the pupil sphere to face outward with a glowing eye and dark pupil, then adding angular brow plates as rotated boxes above each eye for an accent detail before moving to the beak.

Now I'm placing the upper and lower beak as tapered spikes - upper fixed to the head pointing down-forward, lower attached to a jaw bone angled slightly upward to form a joint. Then I'm planning the tentacles: eight main arms spread outward from the body with curled tips resting on the floor, plus two longer raised arms for visual interest.

Working out tentacle paths...

Adjusting the tentacle path points and adding lateral curl offsets using perpendicular vectors, then setting up the joint chains per arm with appropriate counts and parenting to the core body.

I'm defining the body paint with cel-shaded mottled coloring and setting up belly sectors for cream undersides on the tentacles, then working out how to place suckers along the underside sweep curve.

For suckers, I'm placing cream cylinder sticks along the underside sweep at 180 degrees, scaling radius down from base to tip across roughly ten per arm across eight arms—80 small sucker parts total, each with its own tapered geometry. I'm also considering adding dorsal accent plates or glowing orange spots along the top ridge for visual interest.

I'll add small glowing orange spheres scattered along each arm, about seven per arm for 56 parts, keeping glow strength modest since they'll be cached. Then I'm designing two extra raised feeler-like arms rising from the sides of the body, curling upward and outward through several control points to reach about 5.8 units high, pushing the total creature height to around six meters with a spread radius near 5.7.

Thinking about "kraken rising" more, I realize I should add a water surface -- a flat translucent-looking teal disc at the base with a subtle foam ring around where the body pierces it. But this raises a staging problem: the body sits at 1.45 height with tentacles emerging in open air, which doesn't read as "rising from water." I'm considering lowering the whole composition so the core sits closer to the waterline, with tentacle bases dipping below the surface for a more convincing emergence.

To sell that effect, I'll add a tapered waterspout-pedestal column beneath the body -- a lathed shape that's wide at the base and narrows upward into the core, colored teal with foam bands, so the tentacles appear to emerge through swirling water rather than floating in empty space. For the mantle itself, I'm adding glowing orange fin stripes as extruded triangular leaf-shaped fins on each side.

Still working out fin orientation...

Still refining the mantle geometry and positioning, then adding orange accent bevels and stripe details to the design.

Still defining mantle cels and stripe bands... I also want ring panel lines and spikes added along the dorsal sweep for extra texture.

For the mantle tip, I'm thinking of capping it with a small glowing crystal shape, like an icosahedron, positioned near the top end of the mantle for visual flair.

Now I'm moving to the head: building a flattened, slightly scaled sphere positioned in front of the core to form the head mass, then working out eye placement using the head's surface geometry to position them symmetrically on either side of the face.

I'm also sizing the core body sphere and checking how it joins smoothly with the mantle's radius sweep, then considering adding a ring of small mouth tentacles sprouting around the beak for extra detail.

Writing sweep code...

Now I'm thinking about armor details — orange Overwatch-style plates for the head, plus a torus ring for a gorget around the neck connecting head and mantle, sized to wrap around the body without clipping too badly.

Also planning orange cuff rings at each arm's base, placing them along the chain using the arm's tangent direction and scaling the torus radius to match the arm's taper at that point.

For body coloring, I'm setting up cream sectors on the belly using the body's sweep paint system, and considering scattering small cream cone barnacles across the mantle and head surface.

Now I'm building flattened torus rings for water ripples around the creature, laid flat via rotation, plus a thin disc cylinder for the water base beneath everything.

I'm checking texel density for the water surface—mottled paint would spread the texture too thin over such a large area, so I'll switch to flat color for the water and keep the column treatment consistent.

For the column, I'm shaping a lathe outline rising from the base to a tapered neck, giving it a teal-blue flat color and adding a foam skirt ring at the base. I'm also scattering small foam-colored droplet spheres at varying heights and sizes around the water feature for the spray effect.

Now I'm turning to the raised feeler arms — building two chains with tapered radii and orange curled tips, using suckers along the way, and writing a generic helper function to construct each arm from a path with chain bones and radius profiles.

Adding layered sucker detail...

With 10 arms carrying sweeps, suckers, glow dots, and cuffs, I estimate around 290 arm parts plus roughly 60 for the rest of the body, staying comfortably under the 1000-part budget. I'm also adding small orange glow spheres along the dorsal line of each sweep, scaled by radius and embedded slightly into the surface, plus a dorsal ink stripe for visual detail.

Now I'm checking the arm path coordinates against the body geometry to make sure the base points sit correctly inside the core sphere without clipping. I'm computing the spread angles for the 8 base arms, confirming a 45-degree gap keeps their radii from overlapping at the body, and now I'm laying out the point lists for the left and right feelers, mirrored by sign, tracing a curve upward and outward from the head.

Checking the feeler tip placement, I'm considering attaching an orange spade-like ellipsoid sphere at the final joint for a club shape, and verifying the tip radius tapers down smoothly. But I realize the main arm tips end up floating about 0.05 units above the floor instead of touching it, so I need to adjust the tip positions or radius so the lowest points actually make contact with the ground plane.

Adjusting water disc height and position so arm tips sink slightly below its surface for a submerged look, then double-checking the arm point coordinates and radius calculations along the catmull path to make sure the chain joints align correctly.

I'm renaming the arm joints to avoid collisions (switching to letter-based names armA through armH), then defining the head and jaw joints with their parent, position, and aim targets before moving on to the mantle chain.

For the mantle, I'm plotting a Catmull-Rom path curving upward and backward from the core through increasingly tapered radii, ending near a pointed crystal tip at the top.

I'm positioning the embedded crystal near the mantle's tip with a slight tilt to follow the tangent direction, then moving on to defining paint functions for the body, starting with a mottled base color and dorsal stripe accents.

Now I'm writing the mantle's paint function, which checks the sweep angle to place an orange highlight band near the edge and dark bands at regular intervals, falling back to the base body color otherwise.

Scattering barnacle clusters across the mantle surface...

Working out brow plate rotation so the outer edge tilts downward symmetrically on each side, colored in flat orange, then starting on the beak spike geometry using base and tip points.

Adding beak and maw details...

Now scattering water droplet spheres randomly around the arms for a spray effect, then adding paint colors to the core and head spheres, plus dark lidded rings behind the eyes for depth.

Working out the pupil shape and position, using a horizontally-stretched slit scaled to sit flush on the eye's surface, matching kraken-style horizontal pupils.

I'll add a tiny white glow sphere near the pupil for a highlight, then move on to finalizing the eye placement on the bone head, writing the file with metadata, and setting up the cuff geometry using torus shapes positioned along the arm's tangent curve.

Still computing arm point positions...
